title: Optimization Design of Hydrofoil Cavitation Performance Facing Grid Fins and Research on the Mechanism of Cascade Interference
content: In the fields of fluid machinery and ocean engineering, the performance of hydrofoils directly determines the efficiency and reliability of equipment such as ships, underwater vehicles, and hydraulic turbines. Targeting the requirements for efficient prediction and optimization of unsteady cavitating performance of hydrofoils, this study conducts research on hydrofoil optimization design and cascade applications by integrating CST geometric parameterization. After obtaining the cavitation performance parameters of various sample hydrofoils, the construction and optimization prediction of the Kriging surrogate model were conducted, establishing an approximate mapping relationship between hydrofoil geometric parameters and cavitating hydrodynamic performance. Aiming to enhance the hydrodynamic performance of the hydrofoil, the optimization design work was carried out, yielding an optimized hydrofoil with increased leading-edge camber and thickness. The conclusions indicate that the maximum lift-to-drag ratio is increased by 16%, and the hydrodynamic performance is improved under most operating conditions. Furthermore, the optimized hydrofoil was applied to a hydrofoil unit cascade to investigate the mutual interference mechanisms among hydrofoils within the cascade. The study concludes that the optimized hydrofoil can effectively improve the hydrodynamic performance of both the isolated hydrofoil and the cascade, providing a valuable reference for the design of grid fins on underwater vehicles.
